title: Practice partner
privacyNote: This is a practice tool, not a prediction. The real person may respond differently — the skills you build here carry either way.

setup.heading: Practice with {{name}}
setup.body: You'll have the conversation with an AI playing your loved one — it talks back with a real voice and pushes back the way real people do, so the hard sentences aren't new on the day that matters.
setup.voiceOn: 🔊  Voice replies on — tap to practice in text only
setup.voiceOff: 🔇  Voice replies off — tap to hear them talk back
setup.reassurance: You can't hurt anyone here. Sessions save privately to your account so you can see your progress — and you can delete any of them, anytime.
setup.whyTitle: This is practice — and practice is the point
setup.whyBody: This isn't a game you win. Addiction has compromised your loved one's ability to make healthy choices, so the person you'll really face may deflect, bargain, or lash out no matter how well you speak. The partner here won't just give in either — because the real one won't. What changes with every rep is you: steadier nerves, cleaner words, a calmer hold on your ask. That's what walks into the real room.
setup.profileToggleOn: ✓  Practicing with the real {{name}} — tap to use a generic partner
setup.profileToggleOff: Use what I've told you about {{name}}
setup.profileToggleHint: Their own phrases, triggers, and recent incidents shape how the partner pushes back.
setup.familyToggleOn: 👥  Practicing as a family — tap to practice alone
setup.whisperToggleOn: 💬  Whisper coach on — quiet tips while you talk
setup.whisperToggleOff: 💬  Whisper coach off — tap for quiet tips while you talk
setup.suggestedLevel: Suggested from your recent reps: {{level}} — tap to use it
setup.warmupLink: Short on time? Do a 90-second warm-up

guarded.title: Guarded
guarded.desc: Minimizes and deflects — "it's not that bad, I've got it under control."

defensive.title: Defensive
defensive.desc: Argues, never yells — turns everything around on you, keeps score, picks your words apart. Cold, not loud.

volatile.title: Heated
volatile.desc: Explodes — gets loud, swears, gets personal, threatens to storm out. A fight, not a debate.

tearful.title: Guilt-ridden
tearful.desc: Collapses into shame and self-blame — "I'm a screw-up, I ruin everything" — and pulls you into comforting them instead of answering your ask.

chat.intro: Say your opening line to {{name}} — the way you actually would. Hold the mic to speak, or type. You go first.
chat.placeholder: Say it the way you would say it…
chat.micPermissionBody: To practice out loud, allow microphone access. You can also practice by typing.
chat.recordingErrorBody: Try releasing the microphone again before leaving this screen.
chat.turnsDone: Session complete — get your feedback below
chat.error: Couldn't reach your practice partner. Check your connection and try again.
chat.dailyLimit: You've reached today's practice limit. Your practice partner will be ready again tomorrow.
chat.safetyBody: It sounds like you might be carrying something real right now. This matters more than rehearsal — reach out now, any time of day:
chat.openingLabel: Your opening line — tap to use it
chat.introFamily: Take turns talking to {{name}}. Tap who's speaking before each line — hold the mic to speak, or type.
chat.redoLabel: Take this moment again — last time:
chat.lineTrimmed: That was a lot for one line, so we kept the first part. Shorter lines land better anyway — say the rest next.
chat.voiceUnavailableBody: Your recording couldn't be read on this device. Try again, or type your words instead.
chat.recordingTooLongBody: Keep each recording under about two and a half minutes. Try again in shorter pieces, or type your words instead.
chat.abuseTitle: Let's pause the practice — your safety comes first
chat.abuseBody: What you just shared sounds like you're being hurt. You deserve to be safe. If you're in danger right now, call 911. The National Domestic Violence Hotline is free and confidential, 24/7.
chat.thirtySecondsLeft: About 30 seconds left in this recording.
chat.safetyUnknownBody: What you shared matters more than any rehearsal. If you're in danger, call 911. Help is here right now, day or night:
chat.keepPracticingHint: Removes that line and goes back to the practice. Help stays one tap away.

debrief.heading: Coach's feedback
debrief.encouragement: There's no winning or losing here — there's only getting readier. Run it again with a different mood, or a harder one. Every rep makes the real conversation better.
debrief.redoLabel: Go back to just before this line and say it again

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.typedNote: Say your lines out loud next time to get feedback on pace, filler words, and volume.

tips.paceFast: You averaged {{wpm}} words a minute — fast for a hard conversation. Slow down; pauses help your words land.
tips.fillersHigh_one: {{count}} filler word ({{examples}}). A short silence sounds surer than "um" — let yourself pause.
tips.fillersHigh_other: {{count}} filler words ({{examples}}). A short silence sounds surer than "um" — let yourself pause.
tips.youHeavy: {{you}} of your sentences started with "you" and {{i}} with "I." "You" sentences land as blame — try "I feel… when…" instead.
tips.longTurns: Your turns averaged {{words}} words. Long turns start to sound like a lecture — two or three sentences is plenty.
tips.loudPeaks_one: Your voice spiked in {{count}} of {{total}} spoken turns. When they push, try getting quieter, not louder.
tips.loudPeaks_other: Your voice spiked in {{count}} of {{total}} spoken turns. When they push, try getting quieter, not louder.
tips.noQuestions: You didn't ask a single question. One honest question — "What would help?" — invites them in.
tips.paceSteady: Your pace ({{wpm}} words a minute) was calm and easy to follow.
tips.fillersLow: Hardly any filler words — you sounded sure of what you were saying.
tips.iStrong_one: You spoke from "I" {{count}} time — that's how you keep them listening.
tips.iStrong_other: You spoke from "I" {{count}} times — that's how you keep them listening.
tips.questionsAsked_one: You asked a question — questions invite them in instead of pushing.
tips.questionsAsked_other: You asked {{count}} questions — questions invite them in instead of pushing.
tips.steadyVolume: Your volume stayed steady even when they pushed.
tips.shortTurns: Short, clear turns (about {{words}} words) — easy for them to take in.

difficulty.upBody: You've held steady against {{current}}. Try {{level}} next — same skills, more pressure.
difficulty.stayBody: One more rep against {{current}} locks in what you're building.
difficulty.topTitle: You're practicing at the hardest level
difficulty.topBody: Keep repping against {{current}} — or switch to a different mood to keep it fresh.
difficulty.downBody: That one was rough — that's exactly what practice is for. A rep against {{level}} rebuilds your footing.

history.loadError: Your practice history could not be loaded. Please try again.
history.deleteError: This session could not be deleted. Please try again.
history.title: Past sessions
history.subtitle: Your reps, saved. Watch the scores climb.
history.empty: No sessions yet. Finish a practice conversation and its transcript and coaching will be saved here.
history.deleteBody: This removes the transcript and coaching feedback permanently.
history.privacyNote: Sessions are visible only to you. Audio is never saved.
history.trendBody_other: Your last {{count}} full practices, oldest to newest.

situationDesc.none: Nothing just happened — you're the one bringing it up.
situationDesc.said_no: You invited them to get help and they refused. Practice staying warm, accepting the no for now, and planting a seed.
situationDesc.money_urgent: They asked you for money — again. Practice a warm, clear no that still offers help that isn't cash.
situationDesc.relapse_after_treatment: They came home from treatment and used again. Practice responding without shame and naming the next step.
situationDesc.er_aftermath: A scare that ended in the emergency room, and now they're minimizing it. Practice meeting the moment with love, not "I told you so."
situationDesc.arrest_aftermath: They were arrested and want it to go away. Practice letting the consequence stand while you point toward help.

family.heading: Who's in the room?
family.body: Add up to four people. Before each line, tap who's speaking — {{name}} will react to all of you.
family.needTwo: A family practice needs at least two names. Add another person, or turn family practice off to practice alone.

practice.letterLabel: Your letter — read it the way you will on the day
practice.invitationLabel: Your invitation — say it the way you will for real
practice.instructions: Read it out loud. Tap the button to start and again when you're done — {{name}} will react to what they just heard.
practice.truncated: This is longer than one practice delivery can hold, so we'll use the first part. A shorter version will land better on the day, too.
practice.paused: Paused at the time limit — what you read so far is kept. Pick up where you left off, then tap Done.

warmup.heading: Warm up before you talk tonight
warmup.body: Ninety seconds, three exchanges, one quick tip. Say your first line to {{name}} out loud — that's the whole warm-up.
warmup.timeUp: Time's up — finish this exchange and get your tip.
warmup.encouragement: That's the warm-up. Take a breath — you've already said the hardest first words once today.
